gold chalcogenides form in the reaction of gold complexes with HX (X = S, Se, Te) via the non-classic nucleation and growth of supersaturated solutions, and the reaction products are strongly dependent on the HX/HAuCl4 ratio.
the interaction of HAuCl 4 with H 2Se and H 2S in aqueous solutions proceeds via the nucleation and growth of colloidal particles and their coagulation to form deposited products.

gold complexes with chalcogens in aqueous solutions produce colloids and deposits with the composition and structure dependent on the chalcogen content.

Au+ ions are reduced to Au0 by H2Se and/or H2S and then form the “dense liquid” droplets, which grow and coagulate, and the Au0 nanoparticles are finally deposited in a form of AuSe/AuSe1−x−xSx nanocomposites with the Au+ sites being preserved in the surface layer.
